content.comment_body: Hello! I'd like to request a feature. It would be very useful if the text/display block could support a reset input for acknowledging messages such as alarms. This is especially needed when using remote communication—currently, while remote alarms can be reset, without a dedicated reset input, local acknowledgement is still required, which can be inconvenient. My current setup involves creating the alarm based on a condition, then linking it to an acknowledgement-enabled display text in parallel with the set input on an RS flip-flop and a network output block. The remote reset (network input) is connected to the reset input of the RS. However, this results in two separate alarm queues operating independently. It would be much easier if the remote reset could be directly connected to the text block, allowing alarms to be reset from any location and the text to be cleared when acknowledged remotely. Another issue involves the hours counter: it's possible to set only 9999 hours for the memory integer, while the counter itself can go up to 99999 hours. This leads to two problems—you can't set, for example, a 17000-hour (about two years) service interval, and you can't create an automatically resetting hours counter at 99999 hours (roughly 11 years), as it would stop counting at that point. Kind regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing inconvenience because the text/display block lacks functionality for remote alarm resets, which forces them to use complex setups to acknowledge alarms remotely. There are also frustrations with the hours counter, where limits on the memory integer make it difficult to align service intervals and automatic resetting with the full capabilities of the counter.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the ability to remotely reset and acknowledge alarms through the text/display block, as well as to configure hours counters for longer service intervals and automatic resets that match the module's maximum supported value.
